metadata.source: Johannes Schneider: Vāgīśvarakīrtis Mṛtyuvañcanopadeśa, eine buddhistische Lehrschrift zur Abwehr des Todes. Wien : Verlag der Österreichischen Akademie der Wissenschaften 2010. (Beiträge zur Kultur- und Geistesgeschichte Asiens ; 66) (Denkschriften der philosophisch-historischen Klasse ; 394) ISBN 978-3-7001-6722-8, p. 235

children.translated_text: Having risen at the dawn twilight, in a beautiful spot of ground,
seated upon a soft cushion, [one should visualize] in one's heart a moon-disc. // 1 //
The first [letter] of the fifth [vowel group], joined with the second vowel,
combined with a half-moon and a dot, adorned with white rays. // 2 //

children.text: tasya śuklamayūkhais tu tārām ākṛṣya vyomani /
children.translated_text: By the white rays of that [syllable], having drawn <s>Tārā</s> from the sky,
two-armed, white-bodied, holding a boon-granting [hand] and a blue lotus— // 3 //
having worshipped her with devotion through the five offerings,
after the confession of sins, then the rejoicing in merit, // 4 //
and the dedication of that [merit], likewise the taking of the three refuges—
one should recite: '<s>Oṃ</s>, I am of the nature of the vajra of the wisdom of emptiness.' // 5 //

children.text: iti svaparaśūnyaṃ vai dhyātvā yogī vidhānavit /
children.translated_text: Thus, having meditated on the emptiness of self and other, the <s>yogin</s> versed in the ritual method,
upon a moon-disc seat situated in the center of a white lotus, // 6 //
the Goddess <s>Tārā</s>, beautiful, arisen from the seed-syllable described before,
with legs bound in <s>vajra-paryaṅka</s> (cross-legged posture), holding a boon-granting [hand] and a blue lotus, // 7 //
her form like the rays of the autumn moon, resting against a moon [disc] at her back,
adorned with all ornaments, with the body of a sixteen-year-old maiden, // 8 //
the mother of all fully awakened <s>Buddhas</s> and their sons, assuming any form at will—
having meditated on noble <s>Tārā</s>, in her heart a wheel of white radiance, // 9 //
with eight compartments filled with eight syllables,
with the name of the practitioner beginning from the center, placed among the consonant '<s>oṃ hā</s>'— // 10 //

children.text: dhyāyād ekāgracittaḥ san ṣaṇ māsān dṛḍhaniścayaḥ /
children.translated_text: one should meditate with one-pointed mind for six months with firm resolve,

children.text: japed akhinnacittaḥ san mantram enaṃ daśākṣaram || 11 ||
children.translated_text: and recite with unwearied mind this ten-syllable <s>mantra</s>: // 11 //

children.text: oṅkāram ādito dattvā paścāt tāre prayojayet /
children.translated_text: placing the syllable '<s>oṃ</s>' at the beginning, then one should employ '<s>tāre</s>,'

children.text: tuttāre syāt ture paścāt svāhāntaṃ sārvakarmikaḥ || 12 ||
children.translated_text: '<s>tuttāre</s>' should follow, then '<s>ture</s>,' ending with '<s>svāhā</s>'—this serves all purposes. // 12 //
Even by <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Indra</s>, <s>Viṣṇu</s>, the Moon, the Sun, <s>Rudra</s>, the guardians of the directions, and <s>Kāma</s>,
[one whose practice is] unbroken even by a hair's tip conquers death as if liberated. // 13 //
Wrinkles, gray hair, misfortune, disease, and poverty are destroyed;
the suffering of the eight great fears beginning with lions is annihilated. // 14 //
Food, drink, mansions, garments, and the like come unsolicited;
<s>siddhis</s> (attainments) of the sword, eye-ointment, foot-ointment, auspicious vessel, and the like [are gained]. // 15 //
Poetic skill, eloquence, retentive memory, and wisdom utterly pure,

children.text: anyā ca vāñchitā siddhiś cakrād asmāt prajāyate || 16 ||
children.translated_text: and whatever other desired <s>siddhi</s>—all arise from this <s>cakra</s> (wheel-practice). // 16 //

body.translated_text: // The <s>Mṛtyuvañcanopadeśatārāsādhana</s> (Instructions for Cheating Death: The <s>Tārā</s> Practice) is completed. //
